blocks.text: The wish (user, verbatim, in order)

content.value: (1) “We should set different tasks we are working on already very early - as soon as epic start stategizing, it should figure out what tasks its considering - we should be able to see that - and we should be able to see what tasks that are being researched about - and then we should see when its in progress - or is blocked - or finished - we want to see that and have a design language on that in our bp tasks, bp chat, and such.”
(2) “No, we might make an Open one, into considering or researching - when we are considering, then we are cosidering researching, or considering building it etc.”
(3) “Open is just a state - we can consider a task, then delete it - then it will not be open - but if we feel the task is ready- then it will be open.”

Synthesized: a STATE GRAPH, not a funnel — considering / researching / open / in_progress / blocked / done / cancelled-or-deleted. OPEN MEANS READY (the team feels the task is ready; only open is claimable — claim/close CAS and epoch fences unchanged). Births: born-considering (a candidate named the minute it is named) or born-open (today's direct filing, unbroken). Considering carries its object (considering-researching-it vs considering-building-it). Engagement honesty: if the cycle that put a task into considering/researching dies, the state lapses honestly, lease-like. All transitions emit additive mutation_events so every surface streams them live. Two fronts this cycle: FRONT A substrate + one design language across bp tasks TUI, Studio board, web embed, @barkpark/react, bp chat, bp task CLI, brief card; FRONT B the epic-cycle workflow walks its own graph — watching bp tasks during a cycle shows the whole arc from first thought to done.

blocks.text: Direction — two new lifecycle states, one brightness ladder, and a workflow that thinks in public

content.value: The finished experience: you open bp tasks (or /admin/projects, or the web embed, or bp chat) while an epic cycle runs, and you watch it THINK. The strategist names candidate slices and dim dotted circles appear at the bottom of the brightness ladder — born considering, each carrying what is contemplated (research it / build it). Survey picks candidates up and they shift to researching — the one new hue, an active investigation you can see breathing. Decide promotes the survivors to open (the familiar full-white circle: READY) and visibly discards the rest — a kill is a rendered event, not a silent disappearance. Builders claim, spinners spin, checks land. The momentum header grows a thought segment: ‘? N considering · ◎ N researching’ ahead of the in-flight/ready/done counts. Nothing about today's direct filing changes: bp task create still births open, ready still lists open, next still claims only ready work.

Substrate choice (tentative, Decide finalizes): considering and researching become FIRST-CLASS lifecycle_status values — the vocabulary grows from 5 to 7 in the ONE Elixir source (Validation.lifecycle_statuses/0), not a parallel engagement field. Statement 3 forces this: a considered task is NOT open, so modeling it as open-plus-overlay would make it claimable unless the ready query changed — with new lifecycle values the ready/next path (queue.ex ready_query, IN ('open','blocked')) is untouched and ‘only open is claimable’ stays true BY CONSTRUCTION. A small companion content map — engagement: {object: research|build, holder (cycle/worker), ts, note} — carries the considering-object and the honesty lease; the existing TTL sweeper grows a second sweep that lapses dead-cycle thought states honestly (emitting an additive event), reusing the lease-reap pattern rather than minting a parallel claim system (no CAS epochs — thought states are not contended work).

Kill semantics (tentative): ledger-honest by default — a killed candidate becomes cancelled with resolution=discarded and a close_reason, preserving the everything-is-a-task audit trail and the false-done reopen precedent; hard doc delete stays an explicit human verb for pure noise (dups never surfaced). Survey checks precedent and FK/edge consequences before Decide seals it.

Design language (tentative): extend the checklist brightness ladder DOWNWARD — thought is dimmer than backlog. considering = dotted circle ◌ at ~35% foreground (not yet solid); researching = a distinct glyph with the wave's one new hue (violet = investigation — justified under ‘color = state, never decoration’ because researching is an actively-engaged state); open/ready/in_progress/blocked/done/cancelled unchanged. One manifest row per new state, GUI prints the identical Unicode glyph, design/check drift gate extended, ASCII fallback defined. Every surface renders UNKNOWN states fail-open as a dim neutral glyph — the hard rule that makes the rollout safe.

Sequencing spine: Front A lands fully (vocabulary + fail-open rendering on every surface + events) BEFORE Front B starts writing the new states — the workflow amendment is the LAST merge. The AXI wave-2 brief-card collision is handled by sequencing serializer changes after the AXI cycle's work or rebasing onto it, coordinated via task claims. Roster: 10+ builder slices (substrate/migration, engagement lease + sweeper, events, CLI verbs + output, TUI, Studio board, web embed + react, chat, brief card, workflow amendment, spec/docs + drift gate).

blocks.text: Direction debate — three candidates, one winner

content.value: A — new lifecycle states (WINNER): considering/researching join the lifecycle_status enum; engagement map for object + honesty. Wins because the user's own model demands it (statement 3: a considered task is not open), the ready/claim invariant holds by construction with zero query changes, and every surface already keys its rendering off lifecycle_status — the design language extends instead of forking. Cost: touches every enforcement layer (validation, schema select, possible DB CHECK, desk_groups) and every exhaustive status switch.

B — engagement overlay field: lifecycle stays 5 states, a separate engagement field carries considering/researching. Rejected: a considering task would be lifecycle open and CLAIMABLE unless ready/next/sweeper all learned the new field — the invariant would hold by convention, not construction; two axes can contradict (engagement=considering + lifecycle=done); every board must merge two fields to render one truth. It quietly re-creates the funnel the user rejected.

C — staging labels (stage:considering): cheapest, zero schema risk. Rejected as a lie: no enforcement, no events, invisible to the design language spine, and it contradicts ‘Open is just a state’ — a labeled-open task is still open and still claimable.

Sharpest attack on A: blast radius — every exhaustive switch on the 5-value enum (Go TUI theme/board buckets, CLI table, @barkpark/react taskboard, Studio board_live, chat, SDK types, old bp binaries in the wild) could crash or misrender on an unknown status; plus a possible DB CHECK migration; plus COALESCE-default-open paths. Absorbed three ways: (1) the wave's hard sequencing — no engine writes the new states until every surface renders them, and every surface gains an explicit fail-open unknown-state fallback first; (2) the states are purely additive — existing tasks never change value spontaneously; (3) the survey censuses every enforcement layer and every switch BEFORE Decide cuts slices, so the blast radius is enumerated, not discovered.

content.value: WHAT HELD, with proof. (1) Exclusion-by-construction is real: the ready/claim path gates on an explicit allowlist ~w(open blocked) — queue.ex:35 (used :91,:104) AND a second, duplicated copy in claim.ex:26 for targeted claims. New states never enter ready/next with zero query changes. (The duplication itself is a pre-existing desync risk the substrate slice should consolidate.) (2) pr-task-gate needs ZERO changes: scripts/pr-task-gate.sh:91 is an allowlist of exactly one value (in_progress); an open task already fails today, tested in pr-task-gate.test.sh:27,66. (3) The publish wall gates only FIRST-publish; claim/close/lifecycle transitions are direct Repo writes (authoring charter D6) — so per-transition cost is nil; the real wall cost is filing candidates at Strategize. (4) The events layer is free: mutation_events.mutation is an unconstrained text column, the /v1/tasks/events keyset stream is documented and verified kind-agnostic — new kinds are purely additive. (5) Studio's task form is free: schema.ex:570 derives select options from Validation.lifecycle_statuses(), and field_inputs.ex:80-99 renders options generically. (6) cancelled is fully wired for never-claimed candidates: close.ex fencing returns :ok when no claim map exists (close.ex:157-164), and the compactor already treats cancelled as terminal.

AMENDMENT 1 — the 'ONE Elixir vocabulary' framing is incomplete: three enforcement layers exist and the third is unreachable from Elixir. The DB CHECK constraint documents_task_lifecycle_status_check (migration 20260528100000:57-67) hardcodes the 5-value IN-list in SQL. Postgres has no ALTER CONSTRAINT...CHECK — widening requires a NEW migration (DROP + re-ADD). A plain re-ADD takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and full-table-scans documents (ALL types, not just tasks) — the same outage class as the 2026-07 slow-migration incident, different mechanism. Safe pattern: re-ADD with validate: false, then a non-blocking VALIDATE CONSTRAINT. There is NO precedent for this pattern anywhere in the repo's migrations, and prod's documents row count is UNKNOWN (only local dev was counted: 9,345). Verify closes both.

AMENDMENT 2 — the fail-open hard rule is currently violated by almost every surface, in the worst direction. The codebase habit is fail-INTO-open/bright, not fail-to-dim-neutral: Board.bucket/1 catch-all → :open (board.ex:988-997), board_live safe_role → :open (board_live.ex:1091) and col_label/1 has NO catch-all (FunctionClauseError on a new column atom, :3377-3381), web columnForStatus → 'open' (task-board-columns.ts:112-114), react roleOf → 'open' (inline.tsx:158-160), chat rail defaults render as ACTIVE. Only the Go TUI fails to a neutral '·' (components.go:109-121) with explicit unknown→neutral defaults in theme.go and semrole. Consequence: if the new states leak anywhere before that surface's table is updated, a considering task renders as a bright READY circle — the exact lie this epic exists to kill. Front A per-surface slices must therefore both ADD the two rows AND flip each default to dim-neutral, in the same PR per surface; the sequencing law (no engine writes new states until every surface renders them) is confirmed load-bearing, not precautionary.

blocks.text: Direction debate — three candidates, one winner

content.value: A — new lifecycle states (WINNER): considering/researching join the lifecycle_status enum; engagement map for object + honesty. B — engagement overlay field: lifecycle stays 5 states, a separate engagement field carries considering/researching. Sharpest attack on A: blast radius — every exhaustive switch on the 5-value enum (Go TUI theme/board buckets, CLI table, @barkpark/react taskboard, Studio board_live, chat, SDK types, old bp binaries in the wild) could crash or misrender on an unknown status; plus a possible DB CHECK migration; plus COALESCE-default-open paths. Founding wave · opened 2026-07-19 · task-lifecycle-visibility-epic · charter: bp-task-lifecycle-visibility-charter.md (+ rotating slot) · DECIDED, BUILDING

Task lifecycle visibility — the thought states become visible states

STATUS: BUILDING — verify complete (9/9 reported with run-proofs), decisions D1–D18 committed to the charter (598de010d), 8 wave slices + 8 backlog tasks filed and published under task-lifecycle-visibility-epic. Round 1 (s1–s4) dispatches now; s5–s7 after their deps merge; s8 is the wave's last merge.

The wish (user, verbatim, in order)

(1) “We should set different tasks we are working on already very early - as soon as epic start stategizing, it should figure out what tasks its considering - we should be able to see that - and we should be able to see what tasks that are being researched about - and then we should see when its in progress - or is blocked - or finished - we want to see that and have a design language on that in our bp tasks, bp chat, and such.”

(2) “No, we might make an Open one, into considering or researching - when we are considering, then we are cosidering researching, or considering building it etc.”

(3) “Open is just a state - we can consider a task, then delete it - then it will not be open - but if we feel the task is ready- then it will be open.”

Synthesized: a STATE GRAPH, not a funnel — considering / researching / open / in_progress / blocked / done / cancelled-or-deleted. OPEN MEANS READY (the team feels the task is ready; only open is claimable — claim/close CAS and epoch fences unchanged). Births: born-considering (a candidate named the minute it is named) or born-open (today's direct filing, unbroken). Considering carries its object (considering-researching-it vs considering-building-it). Engagement honesty: if the cycle that put a task into considering/researching dies, the state lapses honestly, lease-like. All transitions emit additive mutation_events so every surface streams them live. Two fronts this cycle: FRONT A substrate + one design language across bp tasks TUI, Studio board, web embed, @barkpark/react, bp chat, bp task CLI, brief card; FRONT B the epic-cycle workflow walks its own graph — watching bp tasks during a cycle shows the whole arc from first thought to done.

Direction — two new lifecycle states, one brightness ladder, and a workflow that thinks in public

The finished experience: you open bp tasks (or /admin/projects, or the web embed, or bp chat) while an epic cycle runs, and you watch it THINK. The strategist names candidate slices and dim dotted circles appear at the bottom of the brightness ladder — born considering, each carrying what is contemplated (research it / build it). Survey picks candidates up and they shift to researching — the one new hue, an active investigation you can see breathing. Decide promotes the survivors to open (the familiar full-white circle: READY) and visibly discards the rest — a kill is a rendered event, not a silent disappearance. Builders claim, spinners spin, checks land. The momentum header grows a thought segment: ‘? N considering · ◎ N researching’ ahead of the in-flight/ready/done counts. Nothing about today's direct filing changes: bp task create still births open, ready still lists open, next still claims only ready work.

Substrate choice (tentative, Decide finalizes): considering and researching become FIRST-CLASS lifecycle_status values — the vocabulary grows from 5 to 7 in the ONE Elixir source (Validation.lifecycle_statuses/0), not a parallel engagement field. Statement 3 forces this: a considered task is NOT open, so modeling it as open-plus-overlay would make it claimable unless the ready query changed — with new lifecycle values the ready/next path (queue.ex ready_query, IN ('open','blocked')) is untouched and ‘only open is claimable’ stays true BY CONSTRUCTION. A small companion content map — engagement: {object: research|build, holder (cycle/worker), ts, note} — carries the considering-object and the honesty lease; the existing TTL sweeper grows a second sweep that lapses dead-cycle thought states honestly (emitting an additive event), reusing the lease-reap pattern rather than minting a parallel claim system (no CAS epochs — thought states are not contended work).

Kill semantics (tentative): ledger-honest by default — a killed candidate becomes cancelled with resolution=discarded and a close_reason, preserving the everything-is-a-task audit trail and the false-done reopen precedent; hard doc delete stays an explicit human verb for pure noise (dups never surfaced). Survey checks precedent and FK/edge consequences before Decide seals it.

Design language (tentative): extend the checklist brightness ladder DOWNWARD — thought is dimmer than backlog. considering = dotted circle ◌ at ~35% foreground (not yet solid); researching = a distinct glyph with the wave's one new hue (violet = investigation — justified under ‘color = state, never decoration’ because researching is an actively-engaged state); open/ready/in_progress/blocked/done/cancelled unchanged. One manifest row per new state, GUI prints the identical Unicode glyph, design/check drift gate extended, ASCII fallback defined. Every surface renders UNKNOWN states fail-open as a dim neutral glyph — the hard rule that makes the rollout safe.

Sequencing spine: Front A lands fully (vocabulary + fail-open rendering on every surface + events) BEFORE Front B starts writing the new states — the workflow amendment is the LAST merge. The AXI wave-2 brief-card collision is handled by sequencing serializer changes after the AXI cycle's work or rebasing onto it, coordinated via task claims. Roster: 10+ builder slices (substrate/migration, engagement lease + sweeper, events, CLI verbs + output, TUI, Studio board, web embed + react, chat, brief card, workflow amendment, spec/docs + drift gate).

Direction debate — three candidates, one winner

A — new lifecycle states (WINNER): considering/researching join the lifecycle_status enum; engagement map for object + honesty. Wins because the user's own model demands it (statement 3: a considered task is not open), the ready/claim invariant holds by construction with zero query changes, and every surface already keys its rendering off lifecycle_status — the design language extends instead of forking. Cost: touches every enforcement layer (validation, schema select, possible DB CHECK, desk_groups) and every exhaustive status switch.

B — engagement overlay field: lifecycle stays 5 states, a separate engagement field carries considering/researching. Rejected: a considering task would be lifecycle open and CLAIMABLE unless ready/next/sweeper all learned the new field — the invariant would hold by convention, not construction; two axes can contradict (engagement=considering + lifecycle=done); every board must merge two fields to render one truth. It quietly re-creates the funnel the user rejected.

C — staging labels (stage:considering): cheapest, zero schema risk. Rejected as a lie: no enforcement, no events, invisible to the design language spine, and it contradicts ‘Open is just a state’ — a labeled-open task is still open and still claimable.

Sharpest attack on A: blast radius — every exhaustive switch on the 5-value enum (Go TUI theme/board buckets, CLI table, @barkpark/react taskboard, Studio board_live, chat, SDK types, old bp binaries in the wild) could crash or misrender on an unknown status; plus a possible DB CHECK migration; plus COALESCE-default-open paths. Absorbed three ways: (1) the wave's hard sequencing — no engine writes the new states until every surface renders them, and every surface gains an explicit fail-open unknown-state fallback first; (2) the states are purely additive — existing tasks never change value spontaneously; (3) the survey censuses every enforcement layer and every switch BEFORE Decide cuts slices, so the blast radius is enumerated, not discovered.

(1) Exclusion-by-construction is real: the ready/claim path gates on an explicit allowlist ~w(open blocked) — queue.ex:35 (used :91,:104) AND a second, duplicated copy in claim.ex:26 for targeted claims. New states never enter ready/next with zero query changes. (The duplication itself is a pre-existing desync risk the substrate slice should consolidate.) (2) pr-task-gate needs ZERO changes: scripts/pr-task-gate.sh:91 is an allowlist of exactly one value (in_progress); an open task already fails today, tested in pr-task-gate.test.sh:27,66. (3) The publish wall gates only FIRST-publish; claim/close/lifecycle transitions are direct Repo writes (authoring charter D6) — so per-transition cost is nil; the real wall cost is filing candidates at Strategize. (4) The events layer is free: mutation_events.mutation is an unconstrained text column, the /v1/tasks/events keyset stream is documented and verified kind-agnostic — new kinds are purely additive. (5) Studio's task form is free: schema.ex:570 derives select options from Validation.lifecycle_statuses(), and field_inputs.ex:80-99 renders options generically. (6) cancelled is fully wired for never-claimed candidates: close.ex fencing returns :ok when no claim map exists (close.ex:157-164), and the compactor already treats cancelled as terminal.

AMENDMENT 1 — the 'ONE Elixir vocabulary' framing is incomplete: three enforcement layers exist and the third is unreachable from Elixir. The DB CHECK constraint documents_task_lifecycle_status_check (migration 20260528100000:57-67) hardcodes the 5-value IN-list in SQL. Postgres has no ALTER CONSTRAINT...CHECK — widening requires a NEW migration (DROP + re-ADD). A plain re-ADD takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and full-table-scans documents (ALL types, not just tasks) — the same outage class as the 2026-07 slow-migration incident, different mechanism. Founding wave · opened 2026-07-19 · task-lifecycle-visibility-epic · charter: bp-task-lifecycle-visibility-charter.md (+ rotating slot) · DECIDED, BUILDING

Task lifecycle visibility — the thought states become visible states

STATUS: BUILDING — verify complete (9/9 reported with run-proofs), decisions D1–D18 committed to the charter (598de010d), 8 wave slices + 8 backlog tasks filed and published under task-lifecycle-visibility-epic. Round 1 (s1–s4) dispatches now; s5–s7 after their deps merge; s8 is the wave's last merge.

The wish (user, verbatim, in order)

(1) “We should set different tasks we are working on already very early - as soon as epic start stategizing, it should figure out what tasks its considering - we should be able to see that - and we should be able to see what tasks that are being researched about - and then we should see when its in progress - or is blocked - or finished - we want to see that and have a design language on that in our bp tasks, bp chat, and such.”

(2) “No, we might make an Open one, into considering or researching - when we are considering, then we are cosidering researching, or considering building it etc.”

(3) “Open is just a state - we can consider a task, then delete it - then it will not be open - but if we feel the task is ready- then it will be open.”

Synthesized: a STATE GRAPH, not a funnel — considering / researching / open / in_progress / blocked / done / cancelled-or-deleted. OPEN MEANS READY (the team feels the task is ready; only open is claimable — claim/close CAS and epoch fences unchanged). Births: born-considering (a candidate named the minute it is named) or born-open (today's direct filing, unbroken). Considering carries its object (considering-researching-it vs considering-building-it). Engagement honesty: if the cycle that put a task into considering/researching dies, the state lapses honestly, lease-like. All transitions emit additive mutation_events so every surface streams them live. Two fronts this cycle: FRONT A substrate + one design language across bp tasks TUI, Studio board, web embed, @barkpark/react, bp chat, bp task CLI, brief card; FRONT B the epic-cycle workflow walks its own graph — watching bp tasks during a cycle shows the whole arc from first thought to done.

Direction — two new lifecycle states, one brightness ladder, and a workflow that thinks in public

The finished experience: you open bp tasks (or /admin/projects, or the web embed, or bp chat) while an epic cycle runs, and you watch it THINK. The strategist names candidate slices and dim dotted circles appear at the bottom of the brightness ladder — born considering, each carrying what is contemplated (research it / build it). Survey picks candidates up and they shift to researching — the one new hue, an active investigation you can see breathing. Decide promotes the survivors to open (the familiar full-white circle: READY) and visibly discards the rest — a kill is a rendered event, not a silent disappearance. Builders claim, spinners spin, checks land. The momentum header grows a thought segment: ‘? N considering · ◎ N researching’ ahead of the in-flight/ready/done counts. Nothing about today's direct filing changes: bp task create still births open, ready still lists open, next still claims only ready work.

Substrate choice (tentative, Decide finalizes): considering and researching become FIRST-CLASS lifecycle_status values — the vocabulary grows from 5 to 7 in the ONE Elixir source (Validation.lifecycle_statuses/0), not a parallel engagement field. Statement 3 forces this: a considered task is NOT open, so modeling it as open-plus-overlay would make it claimable unless the ready query changed — with new lifecycle values the ready/next path (queue.ex ready_query, IN ('open','blocked')) is untouched and ‘only open is claimable’ stays true BY CONSTRUCTION. A small companion content map — engagement: {object: research|build, holder (cycle/worker), ts, note} — carries the considering-object and the honesty lease; the existing TTL sweeper grows a second sweep that lapses dead-cycle thought states honestly (emitting an additive event), reusing the lease-reap pattern rather than minting a parallel claim system (no CAS epochs — thought states are not contended work).

Kill semantics (tentative): ledger-honest by default — a killed candidate becomes cancelled with resolution=discarded and a close_reason, preserving the everything-is-a-task audit trail and the false-done reopen precedent; hard doc delete stays an explicit human verb for pure noise (dups never surfaced). Survey checks precedent and FK/edge consequences before Decide seals it.

Design language (tentative): extend the checklist brightness ladder DOWNWARD — thought is dimmer than backlog. considering = dotted circle ◌ at ~35% foreground (not yet solid); researching = a distinct glyph with the wave's one new hue (violet = investigation — justified under ‘color = state, never decoration’ because researching is an actively-engaged state); open/ready/in_progress/blocked/done/cancelled unchanged. One manifest row per new state, GUI prints the identical Unicode glyph, design/check drift gate extended, ASCII fallback defined. Every surface renders UNKNOWN states fail-open as a dim neutral glyph — the hard rule that makes the rollout safe.

Sequencing spine: Front A lands fully (vocabulary + fail-open rendering on every surface + events) BEFORE Front B starts writing the new states — the workflow amendment is the LAST merge. The AXI wave-2 brief-card collision is handled by sequencing serializer changes after the AXI cycle's work or rebasing onto it, coordinated via task claims. Roster: 10+ builder slices (substrate/migration, engagement lease + sweeper, events, CLI verbs + output, TUI, Studio board, web embed + react, chat, brief card, workflow amendment, spec/docs + drift gate).

Direction debate — three candidates, one winner

A — new lifecycle states (WINNER): considering/researching join the lifecycle_status enum; engagement map for object + honesty. Wins because the user's own model demands it (statement 3: a considered task is not open), the ready/claim invariant holds by construction with zero query changes, and every surface already keys its rendering off lifecycle_status — the design language extends instead of forking. Cost: touches every enforcement layer (validation, schema select, possible DB CHECK, desk_groups) and every exhaustive status switch.

B — engagement overlay field: lifecycle stays 5 states, a separate engagement field carries considering/researching. Rejected: a considering task would be lifecycle open and CLAIMABLE unless ready/next/sweeper all learned the new field — the invariant would hold by convention, not construction; two axes can contradict (engagement=considering + lifecycle=done); every board must merge two fields to render one truth. It quietly re-creates the funnel the user rejected.

C — staging labels (stage:considering): cheapest, zero schema risk. Rejected as a lie: no enforcement, no events, invisible to the design language spine, and it contradicts ‘Open is just a state’ — a labeled-open task is still open and still claimable.

Sharpest attack on A: blast radius — every exhaustive switch on the 5-value enum (Go TUI theme/board buckets, CLI table, @barkpark/react taskboard, Studio board_live, chat, SDK types, old bp binaries in the wild) could crash or misrender on an unknown status; plus a possible DB CHECK migration; plus COALESCE-default-open paths. Absorbed three ways: (1) the wave's hard sequencing — no engine writes the new states until every surface renders them, and every surface gains an explicit fail-open unknown-state fallback first; (2) the states are purely additive — existing tasks never change value spontaneously; (3) the survey censuses every enforcement layer and every switch BEFORE Decide cuts slices, so the blast radius is enumerated, not discovered.

Survey plan — 16 scouts

Each question below is a load-bearing assumption of the direction; the answers are ammunition for Digest/Verify, and the substrate question (new-values vs overlay) stays formally open until they land.

What happens next

Survey flies (16 Sonnets) → Digest appends the synthesis + verify plan here → Verify proves the load-bearing claims with run output → Decide seals substrate/kill/glyph choices, writes the founding charter, files the 10+ builder roster (each slice task carries this paper's id) → Build → Review closes this story as the debrief.

Survey digest — 16 reports in; the direction survives, with four amendments

WHAT HELD, with proof. (1) Exclusion-by-construction is real: the ready/claim path gates on an explicit allowlist ~w(open blocked) — queue.ex:35 (used :91,:104) AND a second, duplicated copy in claim.ex:26 for targeted claims. New states never enter ready/next with zero query changes. (The duplication itself is a pre-existing desync risk the substrate slice should consolidate.) (2) pr-task-gate needs ZERO changes: scripts/pr-task-gate.sh:91 is an allowlist of exactly one value (in_progress); an open task already fails today, tested in pr-task-gate.test.sh:27,66. (3) The publish wall gates only FIRST-publish; claim/close/lifecycle transitions are direct Repo writes (authoring charter D6) — so per-transition cost is nil; the real wall cost is filing candidates at Strategize. (4) The events layer is free: mutation_events.mutation is an unconstrained text column, the /v1/tasks/events keyset stream is documented and verified kind-agnostic — new kinds are purely additive. (5) Studio's task form is free: schema.ex:570 derives select options from Validation.lifecycle_statuses(), and field_inputs.ex:80-99 renders options generically. (6) cancelled is fully wired for never-claimed candidates: close.ex fencing returns :ok when no claim map exists (close.ex:157-164), and the compactor already treats cancelled as terminal.

AMENDMENT 1 — the 'ONE Elixir vocabulary' framing is incomplete: three enforcement layers exist and the third is unreachable from Elixir. The DB CHECK constraint documents_task_lifecycle_status_check (migration 20260528100000:57-67) hardcodes the 5-value IN-list in SQL. Postgres has no ALTER CONSTRAINT...CHECK — widening requires a NEW migration (DROP + re-ADD). A plain re-ADD takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and full-table-scans documents (ALL types, not just tasks) — the same outage class as the 2026-07 slow-migration incident, different mechanism. Safe pattern: re-ADD with validate: false, then a non-blocking VALIDATE CONSTRAINT. There is NO precedent for this pattern anywhere in the repo's migrations, and prod's documents row count is UNKNOWN (only local dev was counted: 9,345). Verify closes both.

AMENDMENT 2 — the fail-open hard rule is currently violated by almost every surface, in the worst direction. The codebase habit is fail-INTO-open/bright, not fail-to-dim-neutral: Board.bucket/1 catch-all → :open (board.ex:988-997), board_live safe_role → :open (board_live.ex:1091) and col_label/1 has NO catch-all (FunctionClauseError on a new column atom, :3377-3381), web columnForStatus → 'open' (task-board-columns.ts:112-114), react roleOf → 'open' (inline.tsx:158-160), chat rail defaults render as ACTIVE. Only the Go TUI fails to a neutral '·' (components.go:109-121) with explicit unknown→neutral defaults in theme.go and semrole. Consequence: if the new states leak anywhere before that surface's table is updated, a considering task renders as a bright READY circle — the exact lie this epic exists to kill. Front A per-surface slices must therefore both ADD the two rows AND flip each default to dim-neutral, in the same PR per surface; the sequencing law (no engine writes new states until every surface renders them) is confirmed load-bearing, not precautionary.

AMENDMENT 3 — 'the ONE token manifest' is actually TWO parallel manifests plus an ungated hand copy. Primary: design/tokens.json `lifecycle` (7 rows incl. derived ready + alias closed), generator design/emit.mjs (LIFE_ORDER :149-151) emitting 4 mirrors (taskboard tokens_gen.go, semrole, paper-surface.css .bp-lg--*, Studio tokens_gen.ex + root.html.heex), gated by design/check.mjs Part B. Secondary: design/status-manifest.json (6 roles, CLOSED 4-tone enum info/ok/warn/danger) feeding Elixir Render.StatusVocab (@canonical status-vocabulary) + Go pdrender, gated by scripts/status-manifest-check.sh — which does NOT cover js/packages/react/src/inline.tsx STATUS_ROLES, a hand-copied table whose own comment admits it is ungated. Web adds 4 more hardcoded spots (column order, columns literal, columnForStatus, a SEPARATE TASK_BOARD_GLYPHS map). Violet for researching is free-form hex in tokens.json (no enum conflict); it only needs tone-enum surgery IF task lifecycle actually flows through StatusVocab — caller trace unresolved, verify closes it. Glyph facts: ◌ U+25CC already ships (instanceLifecycle.provisioning) — proven safe; ◎ U+25CE has ZERO precedent in the repo — unproven; glyph_budget_test.go's closed allowlist will red CI until extended (by design).

AMENDMENT 4 — the AXI wave-2 collision, as premised, does not exist today. AXI wave 1 is fully merged (PRs #4152-4158, #4165, all 7 slices done); no wave-2 tasks are filed; the 5 open axi-b* backlog tasks touch nothing in the brief card; zero open PRs touch any target file (only #2907, unrelated); zero active claims exist ledger-wide at survey time. The brief-card slice is UNBLOCKED — it needs only a claim-check at build start. The REAL live watch item is unnamed by the wish: wsc-bl-agent-task-join (open, unclaimed, Wave session-card epic) declares files including api/lib/barkpark/tasks/prime.ex and deep-links board_live.ex — this epic's substrate/board slices must declare files: labels on prime.ex + board_live.ex and check its claim state. Caveat: the ledger scan capped at 500 docs and pagination stalled; verify sweeps the full ledger.

KILL SEMANTICS — evidence backs ledger-honest cancel, and surfaces a new load-bearing gap. cancelled+close_reason is ratified substrate: schema.ex:676-689 already REQUIRES a non-empty close_reason for cancelled, and an outcome.resolution enum exists (shipped/fixed/partial/wont_do/duplicate/superseded — no 'discarded' yet; adding it is a small additive schema edit Decide must explicitly scope). Hard delete's landmines are proven: a dangling id in another task's content.dependencies fails the readiness gate CLOSED forever with no repair sweep (queue.ex:15,:127-141 — comment names 'including a dangling id'); mutation_events rows survive but dangle (doc_id is plain text, no FK); pr-task-gate treats 404 as definitive fail. NEWLY LOAD-BEARING PRE-EXISTING GAP: dependency axis-2 only satisfies on lifecycle_status='done' — so a legitimately CANCELLED blocker ALSO strands its dependents forever. Whatever kill semantics Decide picks, it must rule on this (cancelled-satisfies carve-out vs kill-time dependents warning vs explicit deferral).

FRONT B mechanics settled by reading the whole workflow file (598 lines). Filing candidates at Strategize requires genuine code edits, not prompt tweaks: STRATEGY_SCHEMA gains candidates[] (additionalProperties:false forces it), SURVEY/VERIFY schemas gain task_id linkage AND their literal 'no bp mutations' sentences (lines 319, 380) need one narrow named carve-out, PLAN_SCHEMA gains candidates_resolved[] for visible kills. Promotion is cheap: wave[].task_id already tolerates a pre-existing published task ('you created or verified it'), so promote = patch the same doc to open. Boards read the PUBLISHED ledger only (LIVENESS_BLOCK:76) — candidates must be published at birth; the draft escape hatch is a dead end (invisible on exactly the surfaces this epic serves). The authoring rubric needs a considering-tier AC relaxation or Strategize fabricates fake proof obligations. ALSO ESTABLISHED. No transition-legality gate exists ANYWHERE at the write layer — board.ex restage_plan is drag-UI-only; a raw patch can flip done→open today (validator checks membership, not transitions). The wave must either build the seam at the write boundary (Content.Writer / Tasks core) or explicitly accept engine-discipline-only; per-verb-only enforcement would be bypassable exactly like restage_plan is. — TTL sweeper: second sweep is NEW code reusing the pattern (advisory lock family 'task:<doc_id>', re-check under lock, CAS rev, additive event) with NO claim epochs; own shorter TTL key; lapse researching→considering (one rung), clear engagement on idle considering (no auto-cancel — kills are human/Decide verbs); pulse.ex proves not every lease write needs epoch fencing. — Chat renders task IDENTITY, not state: the Studio chip payload already carries lifecycle_status (mcp_tasks.go) so chip coloring is a cheap Front-A add; live per-task transition streaming is NEW plumbing on BOTH chat surfaces (no mutation_events subscription exists) and must be its own slice; the epic wave_status heartbeat line (already rendered GUI+TUI) is the cheap aggregate hook for '? N considering · ◎ N researching'. — Web embed + @barkpark/react task-board are STATIC snapshot emitters (no live component exists; no refresh wiring found) — 'streams live' must be honestly scoped per surface. — Brief card: additive-safe (no Go strict decode of task docs; follow the criteria_progress omit-when-absent precedent for a 14th engagement key; charter decision-3 list goes stale and needs a doc touch). — desk_groups chips: considering/researching would be INVISIBLE in Studio's desk filters — explicit slice line-item. — Design-spec reconciliation: 'ready' is a DERIVED render row over stored open (never persisted; TUI synthesizes it client-side, fetch.go:25) — the spec table must learn a stored-vs-derived distinction or reviewers will read contradictions.

D12 Studio board grows two dim columns at the ladder bottom; considering's object renders as a secondary marker from engagement.object, not a hue split.
